architecture.mechanism: Frequent engine start-stop cycles alter combustion stability and emission chemistry, producing transient torque disturbances during engine re-engagement.
architecture.intervention: Reprogram the powertrain control module to modify the stop-approach deceleration fuel cut-off threshold and engine restart timing logic, preventing premature or unstable engine re-engagement during the final phase of deceleration.
architecture.expected_effect: Elimination of the 3-second unintended acceleration and vibration event during stop approach without triggering a diagnostic trouble code or illuminating the malfunction indicator lamp.
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct controlled dynamometer stop-approach simulations using datalogger-recorded engine speed, throttle position, and wheel torque traces to verify that the transient torque spike no longer occurs under the updated calibration, confirming resolution in the absence of stored codes.
